findings.evidence_snippet: — no aria-label, no title. Same pattern for 'Sandwich Classique'. Both render visibly truncated as 'Sandwich...' in the sidebar grid.
findings.claim: Two sidebar categories ('Sandwich Cayenne', 'Sandwich Classique') render visually-truncated as 'Sandwich...' with neither aria-label nor title attribute. Sighted operators and screen-reader users cannot distinguish them — blocks primary catalogue-navigation task path.
findings.fix_hint: Add :aria-label and :title bound to the full category name on the .pos-v5-category button in the POS V4 sidebar component. Consider also widening the pill or word-breaking to avoid the visual truncation in the first place.

findings.evidence_snippet: After confirm-pay click: orderpayment modal has class 'modal pos-v4-payment-modal pos-v5-payment-modal active' (still open with keypad), while receiptModal has class 'modal pos-v5-receipt-modal' (no 'active' / open-state class). 'Trop de requêtes' toast (role=alert) is visible.
findings.claim: After a successful cash payment (spec captured payRes.status=200, DB order 1324 persisted with fiscal_seq 294), the payment modal does NOT close and the receipt overlay never opens because a subsequent throttled POST surfaces a 429 toast that suppresses the success-handler chain. Operator-visible state shows the cash keypad still open with a 'Trop de requêtes' toast, masking the fact that the order was actually persisted. High risk of duplicate re-confirm clicks (saved by idempotency middleware, but UX is dangerous).
findings.fix_hint: Decouple receipt-open logic from any later 429 fallout — once orderpayment.confirm resolves to 2xx, immediately open receipt modal and clear payment modal. Throttle-related toast should not abort the success flow.

findings.evidence_snippet: S4 spec target = Sandwich Classique (id 477) per wave-B-db-checks.json line 60. Wizard popup screenshot shows item title 'Sandwich Cayenne €7.00' instead. Both items have price 7.00€ so the cart total looks correct, but the persisted item_id and composition_snapshot would diverge from intent.
findings.claim: Spec selector fallback (data-pos-item-id lookup) silently picks the wrong tile in S4 — wizard launches Sandwich Cayenne (id 474) instead of Sandwich Classique (id 477). The GStack report only flagged this for S10, missing S4. Test-side defect, not production code, but invalidates 1/5 scenarios.
findings.fix_hint: Strengthen tile selector in tests/e2e/rush-100-pos-capture.spec.js to require an EXACT data-pos-item-id match before clicking, with an explicit category-pill click first when the target item is not in the 'Toutes les' grid.

findings.state: ALL pos-grid states (37 product tiles per page)
findings.evidence_snippet: All 37 tile images use src='http://127.0.0.1:8000/images/menu/item-default.svg' — a single generic '+' placeholder. No product photo on any tile (Grande Frites, Petite Frites, Bol Gratiné, Big Tacos, Sandwich Cayenne, etc.).
findings.claim: POS V4 product grid renders 100% of tiles with the identical 'item-default.svg' placeholder, eliminating visual product discoverability. Operator must read the small text label below the giant '+' icon for every tile during a busy rush — defeats the purpose of an image-tile grid.
findings.fix_hint: Upload product photos to /storage/menu/items/ and bind tile src to item.featured_image_url with item-default.svg as fallback only. The empty src field is currently null in the DB / response, triggering the fallback for 100% of items.

findings.evidence_snippet: Toast text: 'Trop de requêtes — patientez 30s avant de réessayer.' But the Vue-Toastification__progress-bar element has style 'animation-duration: 6000ms', so the toast disappears after ~6s. The user told to wait 30s but the visual indicator vanishes after 6s.
findings.claim: Copy-vs-behaviour mismatch in the throttle toast: copy says '30s', progress bar animates over 6s. Confusing under stress; user thinks the timer is the throttle window when it is actually just the toast lifetime.
findings.fix_hint: Either extend the toast duration to 30s (Vue-Toastification timeout option) or rewrite the copy to 'Trop de requêtes — réessayez dans quelques secondes' without committing to a specific number.

findings.evidence_snippet: On initial /admin/pos-v4 load, the right-hand drawer 'Commandes borne — à encaisser' is auto-opened over the POS grid, badge '24', listing pending kiosk orders. POS grid is dimmed behind the drawer overlay. Operator must close the drawer before they can ring up a new sale.
findings.claim: Pending-kiosk-encaisser drawer auto-opens on POS V4 mount, blocking the primary 'ring up new sale' task path for operators who don't intend to clear kiosk debt first. S6-01-pos-empty.png shows the drawer correctly closed in subsequent loads — so the auto-open is initial-mount only, but still suboptimal for busy rush.
findings.fix_hint: Make the auto-open behaviour configurable per branch policy, or default to closed with a prominent badge-only indicator on the 'À encaisser 24' button.

findings.evidence_snippet: S10 was designed as a 'multi-cart 3 items' scenario. Cart DOM contains a SINGLE article (pos-v5-cart-item) for 'Sandwich Cayenne' with input qty='3' and line price 21.00€. There is no second/third distinct line item. Per the GStack report the spec selector fallback misfired and the cart only held Sandwich Cayenne ×3 (same product, qty 3), not three different products.
findings.claim: Spec-level: S10 multi-cart scenario was NEVER actually exercised as 3 distinct items — only Sandwich Cayenne added 3 times. Confirms F-W-B-01 in greater depth: the failure is not just 'fallback selector picks Petite Frites' but 'all three additions resolved to the same Sandwich Cayenne tile'.
findings.fix_hint: Rewrite S10 to add three distinct tiles by selecting category pills explicitly (Bol Crousti → Sandwich Cayenne → Salade Royale) before each add, and assert getByText(productName).count() === 1 in cart after each add.

findings.evidence_snippet: S10 db row: id=1325, fiscal_sequence_no=NULL, total=2.5, lines_count=1, composition_snapshot_lines=1, payment_status=15, status=4. Spec target_item=Sandwich Cayenne (id 474, 7.00€), read_grand_total=21 from UI. So persisted total (2.5€) ≠ UI total (21€) ≠ target (7€). Order was created with payment_status=15 (failed/partial) and fiscal_sequence_no=NULL.
findings.claim: An order row 1325 was committed to DB with payment_status=15 (failed) and fiscal_sequence_no=NULL — a NF525 RED-FLAG state: persisted but not fiscal-allocated. Whether this was caused by THIS spec run or an orphan from earlier, the row exists. The GStack report classifies S10 as 'PARTIAL persisted' without flagging the NULL fiscal_sequence — that field being NULL after status=4 (completed) is exactly the gap-with-flag scenario CLAUDE.md §8 mandates a fiscal_alloc_error_at retry cron should catch. Need to verify the retry cron picked it up.
findings.fix_hint: Query SELECT id, fiscal_sequence_no, fiscal_alloc_error_at, payment_status, status FROM orders WHERE fiscal_sequence_no IS NULL AND status IN (3,4,5) — any rows here are NF525 audit liability and must either be retried or marked void. Add an alert when this count > 0.

findings.evidence_snippet: POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/admin/pos → 429 captured in network.json for all 5 receipt states. This is a SECOND post (after the successful 200 that the spec waitForResponse captured), likely triggered by a duplicate click or the tracker-polling cycle.
findings.claim: The /api/admin/pos endpoint receives a duplicate POST after each successful payment, triggering 429 throttle. The first POST succeeds (200, order persisted), the second is throttled. Production-correct (throttle works), but indicates a frontend defect: confirm-pay button is not debounced or disabled after first click, allowing a stray second submission.
findings.fix_hint: In the cash-payment-confirm handler (PosPaymentComponent / vanilla pos-wizard.js), set the confirm button's disabled=true and aria-busy=true at click start and clear only after 2xx response. Verify the throttle wall is hit by retries not by polling.
